title: Satisfiability with two variables and one transitive relation
formal: Is satisfiability decidable for first-order sentences with equality, only two reusable variable symbols, and one distinguished binary relation required to be transitive, when models may be finite or infinite?
definitions:
The input is a finite sentence over a finite vocabulary of unary and binary relation symbols, one of which is distinguished as T. There are no function symbols, constants or counting quantifiers. Only x and y may appear as variables, but quantifiers can bind and reuse them at arbitrary nesting depth. All Boolean connectives and ordinary existential and universal quantifiers are permitted. Equality has its usual interpretation.

A model is any nonempty structure in which T satisfies: for all elements a,b,c, T(a,b) and T(b,c) imply T(a,c). This semantic restriction may use three elements even though the input sentence has two variables. Reflexivity, irreflexivity, antisymmetry and totality are not required. All other predicates are unrestricted. The question is whether a total Turing machine can decide existence of such a model for every input sentence; neither model size nor running time is bounded. An infinite model is a valid witness even if no finite model exists.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked decision algorithm for unrestricted satisfiability or prove undecidability. Deciding only existence of finite models, or only sentences with guarded existential witnesses, does not meet this target.
context:
The finite satisfiability theorem does not settle general satisfiability because transitivity permits formulas whose models must be infinite.

The 2026 partial-order study explicitly identifies general one-transitive-relation satisfiability as the motivation and treats restricted fragments.
why: The target isolates a basic boundary between finite-model and unrestricted decidability.

import_provenance.original_title: Satisfiability with two variables and one transitive relation
import_provenance.original_statement: Is satisfiability decidable for first-order logic using only two variables when one designated binary relation must be transitive and the remaining relations are unrestricted? The question permits infinite models and continues Kieroński’s work on semantic restrictions in two-variable logic.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Finite satisfiability is already decidable (Pratt-Hartmann, 2018); it must not be conflated with this unrestricted satisfiability question: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.05558.
